org: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC)

name.en: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships 2027
name.ka: Commonwealth Shared სტიპენდიები 2027
name.ar: منح الكومنولث المشتركة 2027

deadline_note: CSC portal opens 10 Nov 2026 and closes 16:00 GMT 8 Dec 2026; you must also apply to a participating UK university course, which nominates candidates.

summary.en: Fully funded one-year master's degrees at UK universities for talented students from 43 lower-income Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford UK study. Jointly funded by the UK government and the host university.
summary.ka: სრულად დაფინანსებული ერთწლიანი მაგისტრატურა ბრიტანეთის უნივერსიტეტებში თანამეგობრობის 43 ქვეყნის ნიჭიერი სტუდენტებისთვის, რომლებიც სხვაგვარად ვერ შეძლებდნენ სწავლის დაფინანსებას. მას ერთად აფინანსებენ ბრიტანეთის მთავრობა და მასპინძელი უნივერსიტეტი.
summary.ar: ماجستير لمدة عام ممول بالكامل في جامعات المملكة المتحدة للطلاب المتميزين من 43 دولة منخفضة الدخل في الكومنولث ممن لا يستطيعون تحمل تكاليف الدراسة دونها. تموّلها الحكومة البريطانية والجامعة المضيفة معًا.

about.en:
Commonwealth Shared Scholarships are run by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC) and co-funded by participating UK universities. They pay for a full-time, one-year taught master's degree on a list of approved courses chosen for their relevance to international development.

The 2027/28 round is for study starting by September 2027. You first apply for and secure a place on an eligible course at a participating UK university, then submit the CSC application on CSC Central between 10 November and 8 December 2026. Each university shortlists and nominates its candidates to the CSC, which makes the final selection.

The award is fully funded: tuition, a return flight, and a monthly stipend of £1,712 (£2,000 in London). It targets candidates who could not otherwise afford UK study and who will contribute to development in their home country, which makes it one of the most accessible UK master's scholarships for students from the eligible countries.

en: Full tuition, return airfare and £1,712/month stipend (£2,000 in London)
Applications open 10 November 2026, close 8 December 2026
Approved development-related master's courses at many UK universities

eligibility.en: Citizens of (or refugees from) one of 43 Commonwealth countries, including Bangladesh, Ghana, India, Kenya, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Uganda and Zambia, who live permanently in that country. You need at least an upper second-class (2:1) bachelor's degree, or a lower second plus a relevant postgraduate qualification, must be able to start by September 2027, must not have studied or worked for more than one academic year in a high-income country, and must be unable to afford UK study without the award. Not open to citizens of Georgia or Qatar.

en: Check the 2027 list of participating universities and eligible courses on the CSC website
Apply to the UK university and course and secure an offer
Complete the CSC application on CSC Central between 10 November and 8 December 2026 (16:00 GMT)
Upload passport/ID, full transcripts and two references
The university shortlists and nominates candidates; the CSC makes the final award

costs.en: Covered: full tuition fees, approved return airfare, stipend of £1,712 per month (£2,000 per month in the London area), warm clothing allowance, thesis grant and study travel grant where applicable, plus partial child allowances for single parents.

score_reason: Fully funded UK master's with an open window right now, but limited to 43 Commonwealth countries.

org: World Bank Group / Government of Japan

name.en: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship (JJ/WBGSP) 2027
name.ka: იაპონიისა და მსოფლიო ბანკის ერთობლივი სამაგისტრო სტიპენდია (JJ/WBGSP) 2027
name.ar: منحة اليابان والبنك الدولي المشتركة للدراسات العليا (JJ/WBGSP) 2027

deadline_note: 2027 guidelines (Aug 2026): Window 1 programmes close 26 Feb 2027; Window 2 programmes close 21 May 2027. You must already hold an unconditional offer from a participating master's.

summary.en: Funds development professionals from World Bank member developing countries to take a master's in a development-related field at one of the participating universities worldwide. You need three years of recent development work and an offer from a participating programme.
summary.ka: აფინანსებს განვითარებად ქვეყნებში დასაქმებულ განვითარების სფეროს პროფესიონალებს, რომ გაიარონ მაგისტრატურა მსოფლიოს მონაწილე უნივერსიტეტებში. საჭიროა სამწლიანი ბოლოდროინდელი სამუშაო გამოცდილება და მონაწილე პროგრამიდან მიღების წერილი.
summary.ar: تموّل المهنيين العاملين في مجال التنمية من الدول النامية الأعضاء في البنك الدولي لدراسة ماجستير في مجال تنموي بإحدى الجامعات المشاركة حول العالم. يُشترط ثلاث سنوات من الخبرة الحديثة في التنمية وقبول من برنامج مشارك.

about.en:
The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP), funded by the Government of Japan and run by the World Bank, pays for a development-related master's degree at a list of participating programmes in the US, Europe, Japan, Africa and elsewhere (for example in public policy, economics, health, energy, infrastructure and tax policy).

It is aimed at mid-career professionals, not fresh graduates: you need a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline, a current full-time paid job in development work, and at least three years of such paid work within the last six years. You must already hold an unconditional offer (except funding) from a participating programme outside your own country when you apply.

The 2027 cycle has two windows depending on the programme: Window 1 closes on 26 February 2027 and Window 2 on 21 May 2027. Scholars commit to returning home to apply their skills, which is what makes this one of the best-known routes for public-sector and NGO staff into top master's programmes.

en: Tuition, round-trip travel, monthly living allowance and health insurance
2027 deadlines: 26 Feb (Window 1) and 21 May 2027 (Window 2)
Requires 3+ years of recent paid development work

eligibility.en: Nationals of World Bank member developing countries listed in Annex 1 of the guidelines (not dual citizens of a developed country). Bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline; currently employed full-time in development-related work; at least three years of paid development-related employment in the last six years; unconditional admission to a participating master's programme outside your country of citizenship and residence. World Bank staff and their close relatives are excluded. Georgia appears on the list of eligible member countries in recent cycles; check Annex 1.

en: Choose a JJ/WBGSP participating programme and check whether it is in Window 1 or Window 2
Apply to the university and obtain an unconditional offer (except for funding)
Read the 2027 Application Guidelines and FAQs for your window
Submit one online application with CV (Annex 4 format), diplomas, proof of employment and admission letter
Arrange two professional recommendation letters submitted online by the deadline

costs.en: The scholarship covers tuition, economy round-trip airfare, a monthly living stipend and health insurance; the World Bank does not publish a fixed amount because it depends on programme length and location. Family costs and visa fees are not covered.

score_reason: Fully funded, confirmed 2027 deadlines, but needs 3 years of development work experience.

org: Aga Khan Foundation

name.en: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme 2027
name.ka: Aga Khan Foundation-ის საერთაშორისო სტიპენდიის პროგრამა 2027
name.ar: برنامج المنح الدولية لمؤسسة الآغا خان 2027

duration.en: Full master's; first 2 years of a PhD
duration.ar: كامل الماجستير؛ أول سنتين من الدكتوراه

deadline_note: 2026-27 cycle closed; the official page says the next cycle opens in early 2027. The deadline (historically around March) will be announced then.

summary.en: Postgraduate awards for outstanding students from selected developing countries who cannot fund their studies, paid half as a grant and half as a loan. Master's degrees are the priority; some PhDs are considered.
summary.ka: სამაგისტრო და სადოქტორო დაფინანსება შერჩეული განვითარებადი ქვეყნების გამორჩეული სტუდენტებისთვის, რომლებსაც სწავლის დაფინანსება არ შეუძლიათ: ნახევარი გრანტია, ნახევარი სესხი. პრიორიტეტი მაგისტრატურაა, ზოგ დოქტორანტურასაც განიხილავენ.
summary.ar: منح دراسات عليا للطلاب المتفوقين من دول نامية مختارة غير القادرين على تمويل دراستهم، نصفها منحة ونصفها قرض. الأولوية للماجستير، وتُدرس بعض طلبات الدكتوراه.

about.en:
The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (ISP) supports postgraduate study for exceptional students from selected developing countries who have no other way to fund their education. Master's degrees at reputable universities abroad are the priority, and PhD applications are also considered.

The award is 50% grant and 50% loan. It covers tuition and living expenses for the full master's degree, or the first two years of a PhD; travel and family costs are not covered. The loan needs a guarantor and is repaid starting six months after you finish. Study in the UK and Russia is not funded.

Applications go through Aga Khan Foundation offices or committees in eligible countries, such as Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, the Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania and Uganda, using the eligibility tool on the website. The 2026-27 cycle is closed and the next one opens in early 2027, so this is the moment to prepare documents and university applications.

en: Covers tuition and living costs: 50% grant, 50% low-burden loan
Master's prioritised; first two years of PhD can be funded
Next cycle opens early 2027

eligibility.en: Citizens of selected developing countries where AKF runs the programme (e.g. Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda; diaspora applicants in countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA must originate from these). Excellent academic record, genuine financial need, and admission to a full-time postgraduate programme outside the UK and Russia. Georgia and Qatar are not listed.

en: Use the eligibility tool on the AKF website to check your country and find your local AKF team
Apply to your chosen universities in parallel
When the 2027 cycle opens, obtain the application form from your local AKF office
Submit the form, transcripts, references and financial documents by the local deadline
Attend an interview if shortlisted

costs.en: Covers tuition and living expenses (half grant, half loan). Travel, clothing, furniture and family living costs are not covered. The loan portion is repaid after graduation, with a guarantor co-signing.

score_reason: Large, well-known programme, but half loan, limited countries and the 2027 dates are not out yet.

org: Stanford University — Knight-Hennessy Scholars

name.en: Knight-Hennessy Scholars (2028 cohort)
name.ka: Knight-Hennessy Scholars (2028 წლის ნაკადი)
name.ar: برنامج نايت-هينيسي للباحثين (دفعة 2028)

deadline_note: 2027 cohort is closed. The official site says the 2028 cohort application opens in June 2027; the deadline (usually early autumn) is published then.

summary.en: Stanford's flagship graduate scholarship: full funding for any Stanford graduate degree plus a leadership programme for about 100 scholars a year. The application for students starting in 2028 opens in June 2027.
summary.ka: Stanford-ის მთავარი სამაგისტრო და სადოქტორო სტიპენდია: ნებისმიერი Stanford-ის ხარისხის სრული დაფინანსება და ლიდერობის პროგრამა წელიწადში დაახლოებით 100 სტიპენდიანტისთვის. 2028 წელს დამწყებთათვის განაცხადი 2027 წლის ივნისში გაიხსნება.
summary.ar: المنحة الرائدة للدراسات العليا في ستانفورد: تمويل كامل لأي درجة عليا في ستانفورد مع برنامج قيادي لنحو 100 باحث سنويًا. يُفتح التقديم للدفعة التي تبدأ في 2028 في يونيو 2027.

about.en:
Knight-Hennessy Scholars funds students from any country to pursue any full-time graduate degree at Stanford University (MA, MS, MBA, JD, MD, MPP, PhD and more), while taking part in the King Global Leadership Program with a multidisciplinary cohort.

The award pays tuition and fees, a stipend for living and academic expenses, an annual economy round trip to Stanford and a one-time relocation stipend, for up to three years. For longer degrees such as PhDs, the department funds the remaining years. You must apply separately to both KHS and your Stanford graduate programme; there are no nationality restrictions and undocumented students are eligible.

The 2027 cohort has closed. The official admissions page says the 2028 cohort application opens in June 2027. For the 2027 cohort, applicants needed a first bachelor's degree earned in January 2020 or later; expect a similar seven-year window for 2028.

en: Tuition, living stipend, annual travel and relocation funding
Any Stanford graduate programme, including PhD, MBA, JD, MD
2028 cohort application opens June 2027

eligibility.en: Open to all nationalities. For the 2027 cohort, your first bachelor's degree had to be earned in January 2020 or later (two-year extension for military service); rules for 2028 may change. You must apply to and enrol in a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme in the same year.

en: Read the KHS eligibility and criteria pages
When the application opens in June 2027, submit the KHS application (essays, CV, recommendations, video statement)
Apply separately to your Stanford graduate programme by its own deadline
Finalists attend Immersion Weekend at Stanford before final selection

costs.en: Covers full tuition and associated fees, a stipend for living and academic costs, one economy round trip per year and a one-time relocation stipend, for up to three years.

score_reason: World-class and fully funded, but extremely selective and the next window opens only in June 2027.

org: Schwarzman Scholars / Tsinghua University

name.en: Schwarzman Scholars (class of 2028–29)
name.ka: Schwarzman Scholars (2028–29 წლის ნაკადი)
name.ar: برنامج شوارزمان للباحثين (دفعة 2028–2029)

deadline_note: Official admissions page: US and global applications open April 2027 and close September 2027 (exact day not yet published); applicants with Chinese citizenship apply March–May 2027.

summary.en: A one-year, fully funded Master of Global Affairs at Tsinghua University in Beijing for future leaders aged 18–28. The next application cycle, for the cohort starting August 2028, opens in April 2027.
summary.ka: ერთწლიანი, სრულად დაფინანსებული მაგისტრატურა გლობალურ საქმეებში პეკინის Tsinghua University-ში 18–28 წლის მომავალი ლიდერებისთვის. 2028 წლის აგვისტოში დამწყები ნაკადის მიღება 2027 წლის აპრილში იწყება.
summary.ar: ماجستير في الشؤون العالمية لمدة عام بتمويل كامل في جامعة تسينغهوا ببكين لقادة المستقبل بعمر 18–28 عامًا. تُفتح دورة التقديم التالية للدفعة التي تبدأ في أغسطس 2028 في أبريل 2027.

about.en:
Schwarzman Scholars is a one-year, fully funded Master of Global Affairs at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University, Beijing. It brings together a cohort of students from around the world for courses on leadership, global affairs and China's role in the world, plus mentors, guest speakers and travel within China.

Any undergraduate field is welcome. Applicants must be at least 18 and under 29 on 1 August of the enrolment year, hold a bachelor's degree by then, and show English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge or Duolingo, unless they studied in English). Selection looks for leadership potential, intellectual ability and character, with interviews for finalists.

The class of 2027-28 is closed. For the class starting in August 2028, the official site says US and global applications open in April 2027 and close in September 2027, with interviews in October–November 2027. Applicants with Chinese citizenship apply between March and May 2027.

en: Fully funded one-year master's at Tsinghua University
Any academic background, ages 18–28
Next global window: April–September 2027

eligibility.en: Any nationality. Undergraduate degree (or on track to finish) before 1 August 2028; age at least 18 and under 29 on 1 August 2028; English proficiency test unless you studied two years in English at undergraduate level or a master's in English. Chinese citizens (mainland, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan) use the separate China application system.

en: Attend an information session and read the application instructions
Prepare essays, CV, transcripts, English test score and three recommendation letters
Submit the online application between April and September 2027
Finalists are interviewed in October–November 2027

costs.en: Schwarzman Scholars describes the programme as fully funded: tuition and programme costs are paid by the scholarship. Check the official FAQ for the full list of what is included.

score_reason: Prestigious and fully funded, but very selective and the next window opens in April 2027.

org: Mundus Journalism consortium (Aarhus University, DMJX, University of Amsterdam, Charles University, City St George's, LMU Munich)

name.en: Erasmus Mundus Journalism, Media and Globalisation 2027–2029
name.ka: Erasmus Mundus: ჟურნალისტიკა, მედია და გლობალიზაცია 2027–2029
name.ar: إيراسموس موندوس: الصحافة والإعلام والعولمة 2027–2029

deadline_note: Official application process page: application period 1 Nov 2026 to 10 Jan 2027, 13:00 CET; one application covers scholarship consideration.

summary.en: A two-year joint master's in journalism across Aarhus, Amsterdam, London, Munich and Prague for graduates with journalism experience. 10–15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover tuition and pay €1,400 a month.
summary.ka: ორწლიანი ერთობლივი მაგისტრატურა ჟურნალისტიკაში ორჰუსში, ამსტერდამში, ლონდონში, მიუნხენსა და პრაღაში ჟურნალისტური გამოცდილების მქონე კურსდამთავრებულებისთვის. 10–15 Erasmus Mundus სტიპენდია ფარავს სწავლის საფასურს და იხდის თვეში €1,400-ს.
summary.ar: ماجستير مشترك لمدة عامين في الصحافة بين آرهوس وأمستردام ولندن وميونخ وبراغ لخريجين ذوي خبرة صحفية. تغطي 10–15 منحة إيراسموس موندوس الرسوم وتدفع 1,400 يورو شهريًا.

about.en:
Mundus Journalism is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's that starts in Aarhus, Denmark (Aarhus University and the Danish School of Media and Journalism) and continues in a second-year specialisation in Amsterdam, London (City St George's), Munich (LMU) or Prague (Charles University). It combines journalism practice with research on media and globalisation.

The programme looks for graduates with above-average grades and real journalism experience, documented by an employer statement and three work samples, plus English at C1 level. The 2027–2029 call runs from 1 November 2026 to 10 January 2027 (13:00 CET); results come on 1 March and the course starts on 1 September 2027 in Aarhus.

Around 10–15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships go to the highest-ranked applicants of any nationality, with no separate scholarship form. They waive the €21,000 non-EU tuition and pay €1,400 a month for up to 24 months, including health and liability insurance.

en: Study in Denmark plus a second year in Amsterdam, London, Munich or Prague
10–15 full scholarships: tuition waiver + €1,400/month
Deadline 10 January 2027

eligibility.en: Open to all nationalities. Bachelor's degree with above-average results, documented journalism work experience (employer statement plus three work samples), English at CEFR C1 (test or approved waiver), two reference letters (one academic, one professional). Former Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders are not eligible for a second scholarship.

en: Register in the online registration form from 1 November 2026
Choose your binding Year 2 specialisation
Compile one PDF package: application form, CV, academic documents, journalism documents, language proof, two references
Upload the package and passport copy before 10 January 2027, 13:00 CET

costs.en: Tuition for non-EU students is €9,000 (year 1) + €12,000 (year 2); EU/EEA students pay only year 2 (€12,000). Erasmus Mundus scholars get a full tuition waiver, €1,400 per month for up to 24 months and free health and liability insurance.

score_reason: Fully funded, confirmed deadline, open to all nationalities; needs journalism experience.

name.en: European Master in Law and Economics (EMLE) 2027/28
name.ka: ევროპული მაგისტრატურა სამართალსა და ეკონომიკაში (EMLE) 2027/28
name.ar: الماجستير الأوروبي في القانون والاقتصاد (EMLE) 2027/28

deadline_note: Official EMLE application page: non-European applicants by 31 Dec 2026, European applicants by 15 Jan 2027 (23:59 CET). Scholarships go to top-ranked complete applications.

summary.en: A one-year master's in law and economics across Rotterdam, Ghent, Aix-en-Provence, Barcelona, Rome, Hamburg, Warsaw, Mumbai and Haifa. About 15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships pay up to €1,400 a month.
summary.ka: ერთწლიანი მაგისტრატურა სამართალსა და ეკონომიკაში როტერდამში, გენტში, ექს-ან-პროვანსში, ბარსელონაში, რომში, ჰამბურგში, ვარშავაში, მუმბაისა და ჰაიფაში. დაახლოებით 15 Erasmus Mundus სტიპენდია თვეში €1,400-მდე იხდის.
summary.ar: ماجستير لمدة عام في القانون والاقتصاد بين روتردام وغنت وإكس أون بروفانس وبرشلونة وروما وهامبورغ ووارسو ومومباي وحيفا. نحو 15 منحة إيراسموس موندوس تدفع حتى 1,400 يورو شهريًا.

about.en:
The European Master in Law and Economics (EMLE) is a one-year (three terms, 60 ECTS), English-taught Erasmus Mundus programme on the economic analysis of law. Students spend terms at two or three of nine partner universities in Rotterdam, Ghent, Aix-en-Provence, Barcelona, Rome, Hamburg, Warsaw, Mumbai and Haifa, and graduate with multiple degrees.

It suits graduates in law or economics, and others who can show a strong interest in law and economics in their motivation letter. You need at least 240 ECTS of prior higher education; final-year students may apply if they graduate before July 2027.

Applications for 2027/28 opened on 1 September 2026. Non-European applicants must apply by 31 December 2026 and European applicants by 15 January 2027. About 15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships (roughly 10 open to all, 5 for target regions) pay up to €1,400 a month; there are also two EMLE Outreach tuition waivers for future teachers of law and economics.

en: Study in 2–3 of 9 cities in Europe, India and Israel
About 15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships, up to €1,400/month
Non-European deadline 31 December 2026

eligibility.en: Any nationality. At least 240 ECTS (or equivalent) of prior higher education, ideally in law and/or economics; final-year students eligible if they graduate before July 2027. English proficiency (e.g. TOEFL iBT 95 or IELTS 7.0 with 6.0 per section) is required after admission unless exempt. Dual citizens must pick one category (European or non-European).

en: Create an account in the EMLE online application
Upload degree certificate and transcripts, a one-page motivation letter and proof of residence
Ask one or two recommenders to send the EMLE recommendation form from a professional email
Tick the scholarship box and submit by 31 Dec 2026 (non-European) or 15 Jan 2027 (European)

costs.en: Tuition: €12,000 (non-European) or €7,500 (European) for the year. Erasmus Mundus scholarships pay up to €1,400 per month for travel, visa, installation and living costs. The EMLE Outreach Scholarship gives up to two full tuition waivers.

score_reason: Short, prestigious Erasmus Mundus programme with a confirmed deadline.

about.en:
The NOHA Joint Master's in International Humanitarian Action is a two-year, 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus programme offered by Aix-Marseille Université, the University of Malta, the University of Groningen, Ruhr-Universität Bochum, Universidad de Deusto, University College Dublin, the University of Warsaw and Uppsala University. Students study at two of them, then do a third semester at a partner institution worldwide or a work placement.

The curriculum covers humanitarian law, anthropology, medicine and public health, management and geopolitics, preparing graduates for NGOs, UN agencies and governments working in crises.

For the 2027–2029 cohort, 16 Erasmus Mundus scholarships are on offer (4 for programme-country, 8 for partner-country and 4 for targeted-region candidates), each €1,400 a month for up to 24 months. Scholarship applicants must submit everything by 15 December 2026 and must already have graduated by then.

en: Two European universities plus a global third semester or placement
16 Erasmus Mundus scholarships, €1,400/month for 24 months
Scholarship deadline 15 December 2026

eligibility.en: Any nationality. A first-cycle degree (at least 180 ECTS) in a relevant field, completed before the scholarship deadline; English at C1 (TOEFL iBT, IELTS or Cambridge) unless exempt; full-time study only. Former Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders cannot apply for the scholarship.

en: Read the 2027–2029 call on the NOHA website
Choose your two universities
Submit the online application at apply.nohanet.org with all documents
Meet the 15 December 2026 deadline to be considered for a scholarship

costs.en: Self-funded participation fee: €4,000 per semester. Erasmus Mundus scholarships pay a fixed €1,400 per month for up to 24 months and cover participation costs.

score_reason: Respected humanitarian master's with 16 scholarships and a clear December deadline.

about.en:
MESPOM (Master of Science in Environmental Sciences, Policy and Management) is a 24-month, English-taught Erasmus Mundus programme. Students study at least three of four universities: Central European University in Vienna, the University of the Aegean in Greece, Lund University in Sweden and the University of Manchester in the UK.

It combines natural science, policy and management, and suits graduates who want careers in environmental policy, consultancy, NGOs or international organisations.

Applications go through CEU's online system. Anyone seeking financial aid, and applicants from visa-sensitive countries, must apply by 7 January 2027; final decisions come on 4 April 2027. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover participation costs and pay the standard €1,400 a month.

Upload transcripts, CV, essays, references and English test score
Request financial aid and submit by 7 January 2027

costs.en: Erasmus Mundus scholars receive a full participation-cost waiver plus a monthly allowance (EU standard €1,400 per month for up to 24 months). Self-funded students pay participation fees listed on the MESPOM finances page.

about.en:
Mundus MAPP is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Master of Public Policy run by Central European University (Vienna), the Institut Barcelona d'Estudis Internacionals (IBEI), the International Institute of Social Studies of Erasmus University Rotterdam (The Hague) and the University of York. Students follow one of four tracks: CEU–IBEI, CEU–York, ISS–IBEI or ISS–York.

The programme focuses on public policy in a global context, including governance, development and international institutions, with a study visit in year 1 and a winter school in year 2.

For the 2027–2029 cohort, applicants who want any financial aid must apply by 1 December 2026. EMJM scholars get a full tuition waiver and €1,400 a month for 24 months (up to €33,600); one institutional 50% tuition waiver per track is also offered. Health insurance is provided by the consortium.

EMJM scholarship: full tuition waiver + up to €33,600

about.en:
Europubhealth+ is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in public health. Students spend year 1 at one university and year 2 at another, choosing one of seven specialisations, and graduate with a double degree. Partners are University College Dublin, EHESP (France), the University of Granada with EASP (Spain), the University of Liège, Maastricht University, Jagiellonian University in Kraków, the University of Sheffield and the University of Bordeaux.

Depending on the pathway, teaching is in English, Spanish or French. It suits graduates in health, social sciences, life sciences and related fields who want careers in health policy, epidemiology or health systems.

Scholarship applications for the 2027 intake close on 8 January 2027 (13:00 CET), with 15-minute online interviews for shortlisted candidates on 18 February. Scholarships pay up to €1,400 a month, include health insurance and cover participation fees; fewer than 1% of applicants receive one.

about.en:
EMMIR is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's on migration and intercultural relations. Edition 14 (2027–2029) starts at the Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg, Germany, and continues with partner universities in Norway, the Czech Republic, Slovenia, Ghana, Uganda, South Africa and India, so students experience migration questions in the Global North and South.

It suits graduates in social sciences, humanities, law or related fields who want to work on migration, refugees and diversity in research, NGOs or public institutions.

Scholarship and non-fee-paying places close on 20 December 2026; fee-paying places remain open until filled (latest 15 July 2027). A very limited number of Erasmus Mundus scholarships pay €1,400 a month for 24 months and cover health insurance and registration fees; merit-based non-fee-paying places waive the €4,500 per semester participation cost.

about.en:
Choreomundus studies dance and other movement systems (ritual, martial arts, games, sport, physical theatre) as intangible cultural heritage, drawing on ethnochoreology, anthropology of dance, heritage studies and dance technology. The consortium is Vytautas Magnus University (Kaunas, coordinator), the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, Université Clermont Auvergne and the University of Roehampton in London.

It suits graduates in dance, anthropology, ethnology, music, heritage or related fields who want academic or cultural-sector careers.

There are no self-funded places: every admitted student receives an EU-funded tuition waiver (worth €18,000), and 17 students also receive a scholarship of €1,400 a month for 24 months. No separate scholarship application is needed. Applications opened on 15 October 2026 and close on 15 January 2027.

GrEnFIn (Greening Energy Market and Finance) is a 24-month, 120 ECTS Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by the University of Bologna with LMU Munich and Université Paris Dauphine–PSL. It trains quantitative specialists for the energy transition: energy markets, climate risk, sustainable finance and the mathematics behind them.

It targets graduates in mathematics, physics, economics, statistics, computer science or engineering with English at least at B2.

The 2027-28 call closes on 7 January 2027 for both EU and non-EU candidates. Erasmus Mundus scholarships go to the best-qualified applicants and follow the EU standard of €1,400 per month plus coverage of participation costs.

summary.ar: المنحة الحكومية الرئيسية في اليابان للدراسات العليا: ماجستير أو دكتوراه بلا رسوم في جامعة يابانية مع مخصص شهري نحو 144,000–145,000 ين وتذاكر سفر ذهابًا وإيابًا. يتم التقديم عبر السفارة اليابانية في بلدك، عادة في أبريل–مايو.

about.en:
The MEXT (Monbukagakusho) Research Student scholarship funds international graduates to study at Japanese universities, either directly in a master's or doctoral programme or first as a non-degree research student before entering one. Fields cover almost all disciplines, and programmes can be in English or Japanese.

The embassy-recommendation route is the most accessible: Japanese embassies and consulates recruit between April and May of the year before arrival, run document screening, a written test and interview between May and July, and recommend candidates to MEXT, who then places them with universities. Applicants for the 2027 cycle had to be born on or after 2 April 1992; for the 2028 cycle the limit normally moves forward by one year.

The scholarship waives entrance and tuition fees, pays 144,000 yen a month for master's students (145,000 yen for doctoral students; 143,000 yen for non-regular research students) and provides economy flights to and from Japan. It is one of the most complete government scholarships in Asia and is open to citizens of almost every country, including Georgia and Qatar.

en: Tuition waived + ¥144,000/month (master's) or ¥145,000/month (PhD)
Return economy flights to Japan
Apply via the Japanese embassy, usually April–May 2027

eligibility.en: Nationals of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan (including Georgia and Qatar). Age limit: for the 2027 cycle, born on or after 2 April 1992 (expect one year later for 2028). Bachelor's degree (or expected) with good grades, a research plan in your field, and willingness to learn Japanese. Each embassy may add requirements such as language tests.

en: Watch your local Japanese embassy or consulate website from early 2027
Download the Research Student application guidelines and forms from Study in Japan
Prepare the application form, placement preference form, research plan, health certificate and recommendation letter
Submit to the embassy (never directly to MEXT) by its deadline
Take the embassy's written exams and interview (May–July)
If recommended, contact Japanese professors and obtain a letter of provisional acceptance

costs.en: Covered: entrance exam, matriculation and tuition fees; monthly allowance of 143,000 yen (research/non-regular), 144,000 yen (master's) or 145,000 yen (doctoral), plus a small regional supplement in some areas; economy return airfare. Amounts may change with Japan's budget.

score_reason: Fully funded, open to nearly every nationality; window opens in spring 2027 via embassies.

about.en:
The Global Korea Scholarship (GKS), run by NIIED for the Korean Ministry of Education, is one of Asia's largest government scholarships. The graduate programme funds master's (2 years) and doctoral (3 years) degrees at over 80 GKS universities, normally after one year of Korean language training; some English-taught master's tracks skip the language year.

There are two routes. In the embassy track (about 800 places), you apply to the Korean embassy in your country, which forwards selected candidates to NIIED and universities. In the university track (about 1,200 places, including general, regional R-GKS and research tracks), you apply directly to a participating university. NIIED announces the programme in February, applications run February–March, and final results come in June, for study from September.

The award covers round-trip airfare, Korean language training fees, full tuition and a monthly allowance, plus settlement and research support. Applicants must be under 40, hold a bachelor's (for master's) or master's (for PhD), and have a GPA of at least 80%.

en: Airfare, tuition, Korean language year and monthly allowance
About 1,600 graduate places across 80+ universities
Announced in February; apply February–March 2027

eligibility.en: You and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship. Under 40 years old as of 1 September of the selection year. Bachelor's degree (for master's) or master's degree (for PhD) completed by 1 September. GPA of at least 80% (or equivalent) in your most recent programme. Good health. Each country has an embassy-track quota; Georgia and Qatar citizens should check the country list in the 2027 guidelines.

en: Download the 2027 GKS graduate guidelines when NIIED publishes them in February
Choose the embassy track (apply to the Korean embassy) or university track (apply to one GKS university)
Prepare application forms, study plan, recommendation letters, transcripts and apostilled diplomas
Submit between February and March 2027
Pass embassy/university screening and NIIED review; final results in June

costs.en: Covered: round-trip economy airfare, Korean language training fees, full tuition, a monthly living allowance, settlement allowance and research support. NIIED publishes the current amounts in each year's guidelines.

score_reason: Fully funded and large, open to most countries; the 2027 call comes in February.

summary.en: DAAD scholarship for a full doctorate at a German university: €1,400 a month for up to four years, plus insurance, travel and research allowances. Mainly for applicants from developing and emerging countries.
summary.ka: DAAD-ის სტიპენდია გერმანულ უნივერსიტეტში სრული დოქტორანტურისთვის: თვეში €1,400 ოთხ წლამდე, დაზღვევით, მგზავრობისა და კვლევის დანამატებით. ძირითადად განვითარებადი და განვითარებადი ეკონომიკის ქვეყნების კანდიდატებისთვის.
summary.ar: منحة DAAD لدكتوراه كاملة في جامعة ألمانية: 1,400 يورو شهريًا لمدة تصل إلى أربع سنوات مع التأمين وبدلات السفر والبحث. موجهة أساسًا للمتقدمين من الدول النامية والناشئة.

about.en:
DAAD's Research Grants – Doctoral Programmes in Germany fund international graduates to complete a whole PhD at a German university or research institute, either in an individual doctorate with a supervisor or in a structured doctoral programme.

You need an above-average master's (or, exceptionally, bachelor's) degree completed by the start of funding, normally no more than six years old at the deadline, a research proposal and confirmation of supervision from a German professor. If you have already started a doctorate, it should have begun no more than three years before applying, and you must not have lived in Germany for more than 15 months.

The current round (funding starting 2027) is closed. The portal opens again on 1 June 2027 for funding starting in 2028, with country-specific deadlines that usually follow the previous year's pattern (often autumn). The grant pays €1,400 a month, a €460 annual research allowance, insurance, travel and German-language support, with rent and family allowances possible.

en: €1,400/month for up to 4 years
Insurance, travel, research and language allowances
Next portal opens 1 June 2027

eligibility.en: Mainly nationals of developing and emerging countries listed in the DAAD database for this programme (check your country of origin in the database). Above-average master's degree completed by funding start, normally not more than six years old; supervision agreement from a German host; not more than 15 months' residence in Germany at the deadline. Medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine follow separate rules.

en: Find a supervisor or structured doctoral programme in Germany and obtain written confirmation
Check your country's deadline in the DAAD scholarship database from June 2027
Register in the DAAD portal and generate the recommendation form for a professor
Upload CV, motivation letter, research proposal, supervision letter, degrees and transcripts
Submit before 24:00 CET on your deadline

costs.en: €1,400 per month, €460 per year research allowance, health/accident/liability insurance contributions, travel allowance on request, language course costs, plus possible monthly rent subsidy and family allowance.

score_reason: Generous full PhD funding; next window opens June 2027 with country-specific deadlines.

about.en:
EPOS (Development-Related Postgraduate Courses) is a DAAD scholarship scheme funded by the German development ministry (BMZ). It pays for professionals from developing and emerging countries to complete selected English- (and some German-) taught master's courses in Germany, such as International Health (Charité Berlin, Heidelberg), Global Health (Bonn), Urban Management (TU Berlin), Hydro Science (TU Dresden), Renewable Energy (Oldenburg, Flensburg), Agricultural Economics (Hohenheim) and Environmental Governance (Freiburg).

It targets people already working in their field: you need a four-year bachelor's in the upper third of your class, at least two years of relevant work experience, and a degree normally no more than six years old. You apply directly to up to three courses, which select candidates and propose them to DAAD.

Graduates receive €992 a month (doctoral candidates in some courses €1,400), insurance and a travel allowance, with possible rent and family subsidies. Each course sets its own deadline, listed in DAAD's EPOS deadline list; many 2027/28 deadlines closed in autumn 2026, so check each course and plan for the 2028/29 round.

en: €992/month plus insurance and travel for master's students
About 25 development-focused courses across Germany
Requires 2+ years of professional experience

eligibility.en: Residents of countries on DAAD's EPOS country list (based on the OECD DAC list of developing countries; Georgia is a DAC country, high-income Qatar is not), so check the list before applying. Bachelor's degree (normally four years) in the upper third, at least two years of relevant work experience after it, degree normally not older than six years, not more than 15 months in Germany at the deadline, and English/German proof (IELTS or TOEFL, institutional TOEFL not accepted).

en: Check the EPOS country list and the 2027/28 course list and deadline list on the DAAD website
Pick up to three courses and rank them in the DAAD form
Send the checklist, EPOS form, Europass CV, one motivation letter, employer recommendation, employment certificates, language proof and degrees directly to the course(s)
If the course selects you, DAAD asks you to upload documents to its portal

costs.en: €992 per month for master's students (€1,400 for doctoral candidates), health/accident/liability insurance contributions, travel allowance, and in some cases rent subsidy and family allowance. EPOS scholars are exempt from tuition fees in courses that charge them (e.g. Freiburg).

score_reason: Excellent funding for development professionals, but course deadlines vary and many 2027/28 ones have passed.

about.en:
VLIR-UOS, the development-cooperation arm of the Flemish universities, funds full scholarships for selected International Courses Programmes (ICP) taught in English in Belgium. For 2027–2028 the funded master's programmes include Aquaculture (IMAQUA, Ghent), Food Technology (KU Leuven & Ghent), Marine and Lacustrine Science (VUB, Ghent, Antwerp), Transportation Sciences – Road Safety (Hasselt), Nutrition and Food Systems (Ghent), Sustainable Land Management (Ghent & VUB), Tropical Biodiversity and Ecosystems (VUB, TROPIMUNDO), and one-year advanced master's programmes at the University of Antwerp in Development Evaluation, Globalisation and Development, and Governance and Development.

The scheme prefers candidates working in (or aiming for) higher education, government or civil society who will act as agents of change at home; women are encouraged to apply. Initial-master candidates must be 35 or younger on 1 January 2027 (advanced master's: 45 or younger).

You apply to the programme and tick the scholarship request in the same application. Deadlines differ: 30 November 2026 for TROPIMUNDO, 1 February 2027 for several programmes and 28 February 2027 for others. Results come by mid-May; there are no partial scholarships.

en: Full package: tuition, travel, insurance, board and lodging
Around 10 English-taught programmes at Flemish universities
Most deadlines between 30 Nov 2026 and 28 Feb 2027

eligibility.en: Nationals and residents of one of 25 countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, Niger, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Morocco, Palestine, Bolivia, Cuba, Ecuador, Peru, Indonesia, Philippines and Vietnam. Age 35 or under (initial master) or 45 or under (advanced master) on 1 January 2027. One ICP application per year; no previous Belgian government scholarship or enrolment in Belgian higher education. Not open to Georgian or Qatari citizens.

en: Check the eligible country list and the 2027–2028 programme list on vliruos.be
Open the programme page and note its own deadline
Apply to the programme through the university and request the VLIR-UOS scholarship in the same application
Apply to only one ICP programme
Join the online info session on 26 November 2026 if useful

costs.en: Covers tuition, international travel, insurance and living expenses (board and lodging) for the full 12, 24 or 36 months. No partial scholarships.

score_reason: Fully funded with open calls now, but limited to 25 countries.

summary.ka: ყოველთვიური სტიპენდია €992-მდე (მაგისტრატურა) ან €1,400-მდე (დოქტორანტურა) გერმანიის უნივერსიტეტების უცხოელი სტუდენტებისთვის, რომლებიც კარგ აკადემიურ შედეგებს საზოგადოებრივ ჩართულობასა და დემოკრატიულ ღირებულებებს უთავსებენ. მოსალოდნელია გერმანული B2 დონეზე.
summary.ar: منحة شهرية تصل إلى 992 يورو (ماجستير) أو 1,400 يورو (دكتوراه) للطلاب الدوليين في الجامعات الألمانية الذين يجمعون بين التفوق الأكاديمي والمشاركة المدنية والقيم الديمقراطية. يُتوقع مستوى B2 في الألمانية.

about.en:
The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, a German political foundation, supports about 300 international scholars from more than 50 countries. Its international talent programme funds four-semester master's degrees and full doctorates at German universities, alongside seminars on politics, society and leadership.

It looks for academic excellence plus social or volunteer engagement (ideally in your home country), commitment to democracy and human rights, and interest in political questions. German at B2 level is expected by the start of studies, even for English-taught programmes. There is no age limit; medicine and three-semester master's programmes are not funded.

Applicants already living in Germany apply via the KAS Campus portal by 15 July each year (12:00 CET). Selected KAS offices abroad also recruit; check the website for the current list.

en: Up to €992/month (master's) or €1,400/month (PhD)
Seminars and a network of ~300 international scholars
Annual deadline 15 July

eligibility.en: Mainly non-EU international students. Master's applicants must plan a four-semester master's at a German university; doctoral applicants must be fully admitted to a German doctorate. German at B2 by the start of studies. Strong academic record, civic engagement and commitment to democratic values. Not for medicine, state-exam dentistry or postdocs.

en: Read the KAS guidelines and FAQ
Secure (or apply for) admission to a German master's or doctoral programme
Register on the KAS Campus portal (campus.kas.de)
Upload CV, motivation letter, transcripts, references and proof of engagement
Submit by 15 July, 12:00 CET (or via a participating KAS office abroad)

costs.en: Up to €992 per month (master's) or €1,400 per month (doctorate); optional health insurance subsidy (up to €120/month), family and child allowances, research travel grants, and in exceptional cases up to €750 per semester toward tuition. Semester fees are not covered.

score_reason: Solid stipend with a fixed annual deadline; needs German B2 and admission in Germany.

about.en:
The National Scholarship Programme of the Slovak Republic (NSP), administered by SAIA for the Slovak Ministry of Education, funds mobility stays in Slovakia for international university students, PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists. Master's and PhD students typically come for one or two semesters of study or research while remaining enrolled at their home university.

For master's students, PhD students and researchers
Two calls a year (30 April / 31 October)

Open to most nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar; see the programme's terms and conditions for country-specific rules.

Prepare a study or research plan, CV, recommendation and transcripts
Submit the online application on scholarships.sk before the deadline
Wait for the selection committee's decision (published list of scholarship holders)

The Islamic Development Bank runs several scholarship programmes for its 57 member countries and Muslim communities elsewhere. Two are graduate-level. The M.Sc. Scholarship Program for IsDB Least Developed Member Countries funds master's study in science, engineering, technology, medicine, Islamic finance, project and procurement management, entrepreneurship, supply chain and public policy for citizens of 20 LDMCs, at universities in IsDB member countries ranked in the THE top 1,000. The Merit Scholarship Program for High Technology (MSP) funds three-year PhDs and 6–12 month postdoctoral research for scholars attached to universities or research centres in member countries.

Both programmes pay tuition directly to the university, a monthly stipend matched to local living costs, medical costs, a thesis allowance, return airfare and an installation allowance. MSP applicants are nominated at the institutional level and must return to their institution afterwards.

The 2027–2028 booklets are already published, and applications are submitted online through the IsDB scholarship portal during the application period. Apply to only one programme per cycle.

Master's for 20 least developed member countries; PhD for all member countries
2027–2028 booklets published; apply via the IsDB portal

MSP (PhD/postdoc): scholars from any IsDB member country who work at an educational, scientific or research institution at home, in priority high-tech fields. Qatar is an IsDB member; Georgia is not.

Secure admission at an eligible university (THE/QS top 1,000 in an IsDB member country, or a partner university)
Register on the IsDB scholarship portal and complete the online application
Upload documents and submit before the cycle's deadline; some applicants are interviewed

costs.en: Covers tuition (paid to the university), monthly stipend set by country cost of living, medical treatment/insurance, thesis or research-paper allowance, conference allowance for PhD scholars, return air ticket and installation allowance. Visa costs and family expenses are not covered.

about.en:
The Rhodes Scholarship, founded in 1902, brings exceptional young people from around the world to the University of Oxford for postgraduate study. Scholars can take most full-time master's and doctoral courses in almost any field, and join a residential community at Rhodes House focused on leadership and service.

Selection is by constituency: many countries and regions have their own Rhodes Scholarships, and applicants from countries without one can apply for the Global Rhodes Scholarships. Candidates are judged on academic excellence, character, leadership and commitment to others, with interviews for finalists.

The award covers Oxford fees, an annual stipend (£20,400 in 2025-26), the application fee, visa and health surcharge, two economy flights and a settling-in allowance; a DPhil can be funded for up to three years. Applications for 2027 entry are closed; they reopen in 2027 for 2028 entry.

en: Oxford fees + £20,400/year stipend + flights and visa costs
Most Oxford master's and DPhil courses
Applications reopen in 2027 for 2028 entry

eligibility.en: Depends on constituency: each country or region (and the Global Rhodes Scholarship for countries without their own) sets citizenship/residency, age and degree requirements. Check 'Check your eligibility' on the Rhodes House website when applications reopen. Both Georgian and Qatari citizens can check eligibility under their regional or the Global constituency.

en: Sign up to the Rhodes House mailing list for the 2027 opening
Check which constituency you belong to and its eligibility rules
Prepare a personal statement, academic statement, CV, transcripts and references
Apply online by your constituency's deadline (typically July–October 2027)
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; scholars then apply to their Oxford course

costs.en: Covers Oxford course fees, an annual stipend of £20,400 (£1,700/month, 2025-26 rate), the Oxford application fee, student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, two economy flights and a settling-in allowance.

score_reason: Iconic and fully funded, but closed until 2027 and extremely selective.

about.en:
TROPIMUNDO (Mundus Tropicalis) is a two-year master's in tropical biodiversity and ecosystems. Semester 1 is in Brussels (ULB and VUB), semester 2 is field experience in a tropical region (partners in Kenya, Senegal, Benin, Cameroon, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, the Philippines, French Guiana, New Caledonia and more), semester 3 is a specialisation at Sorbonne/MNHN in Paris or the University of Florence, and semester 4 is the thesis.

It suits biology, natural science and environmental science graduates (about 180 ECTS) with good English, plus French or Spanish as a bonus.

The first call, for scholarship seekers, closes on 30 November 2026. Students from VLIR-UOS countries can receive a full VLIR-UOS scholarship; Erasmus Mundus scholarships for all nationalities depend on European Commission approval. Self-funded applicants can apply from February to 30 April 2027 (tuition €9,000 a year for non-associated third-country students, €4,500 for EU and associated countries).

en: Field semester in tropical Africa, Asia or South America
VLIR-UOS full scholarships; Erasmus Mundus scholarships pending EC approval
Scholarship deadline 30 November 2026

VLIR-UOS scholarships only for nationals/residents of the 25 VLIR-UOS countries; Erasmus Mundus scholarships (if funded) open to all nationalities.

Upload diploma, transcripts, language proof, CV and motivation letter
Indicate that you are a scholarship seeker (VLIR-UOS and/or Erasmus Mundus)
Submit by 30 November 2026

For two-year master's, the same amount can be paid in year two if you reach an average grade of 7/10 and at least 50% of credits by the end of the third quartile. UTS holders can also indicate interest in the Kipaji Scholarship.

You must be in the top 5–10% of your graduating class and have IELTS 6.5 (speaking 6.0) or TOEFL iBT 90. Apply for your master's first, wait for (conditional) admission, then submit the UTS form with your student number between 15 October 2026 and 1 April 2027.

There is no separate scholarship form: applying to the master's in the first call makes you eligible, and each teaching committee ranks candidates on academic merit. The 2027/28 calls are due to be published in November 2026, with deadlines in each programme's admission notice.

about.en:
The ADB–Japan Scholarship Program, funded by Japan and run by the Asian Development Bank since 1988, offers about 130 scholarships a year for master's study at 27 designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, 17 of them in Japan (for example GRIPS, Hitotsubashi, Keio, the University of Tokyo and others listed on adb.org).

It is for early-career professionals from ADB developing member countries: you need a strong bachelor's record, at least two years of full-time work, be 35 or younger, live and work in your home country, and agree to work there for two years after graduating.

You apply to a participating master's programme and submit the JSP information sheet with your application; the institution shortlists and ADB makes the final selection. Benefits include full tuition, a monthly allowance with housing, books, medical insurance and travel.

about.en:
King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals in Dhahran is Saudi Arabia's leading engineering and science university. It awards full scholarships to international graduate students in all PhD programmes and in selected thesis-based MS programmes that do not have a corresponding doctoral track.

Scholars get free tuition, a monthly stipend set by scholarship category, free furnished on-campus housing with utilities, round-trip air tickets and medical and dental care. MS applicants need a four-year engineering or science bachelor's with GPA 3.00/4.00 for scholarship consideration and English (TOEFL iBT 70, IELTS 6.0 or Duolingo 105); PhD applicants need a relevant master's with GPA 3.00 and TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 120. Direct-entry PhD from a bachelor's is possible.

The College of Graduate Studies lists an application window of 1 November to 15 December 2026 for thesis-based MS and PhD programmes, with applications through apply.kfupm.edu.sa and decisions in two to three months.

about.en:
The Fulbright Foreign Student Program brings graduate students, young professionals and artists from more than 160 countries to study and research in the United States, with about 4,000 new grants each year. Most awards fund a one- or two-year master's degree; some countries also fund PhD study or non-degree research.

Everything is run nationally. The binational Fulbright commission or the US embassy in your country decides eligibility, fields, deadlines and interviews, and either IIE places you at US universities (IIE-placement) or you apply to universities yourself (self-placement). Grants typically cover tuition, a living stipend, health coverage and travel, though the package varies by country.

Deadlines for study starting in 2027 have mostly passed. For 2028–29, country calls generally open in early 2027 and close between February and October 2027, so now is the time to take the TOEFL/IELTS and GRE where needed and watch your national Fulbright page. Georgia has its own Fulbright Graduate Student Program run by the US Embassy in Tbilisi.

eligibility.en: Citizens of participating countries (rules set nationally), usually with a bachelor's degree, strong English (TOEFL/IELTS) and, for many countries, a commitment to return home after the grant (J-1 visa two-year home-residency rule). People who already hold a PhD are generally not eligible. Check your country's page for age and field rules.

costs.en: Depends on the country, but grants generally cover tuition and fees (or IIE-negotiated waivers), a monthly living stipend, health benefits and round-trip travel.

Students start in Lüneburg, continue in Barcelona and then choose one of four specialisation tracks, studying in at least three countries.

It covers international law on armed conflict, peace-building, human rights, security and sustainable development, preparing graduates for international organisations, NGOs, governments and research. An LLM track needs 60 ECTS in law; the MA track accepts law, political science, international relations or European studies. English at C1 (IELTS 7.0) is required; the Brussels track also needs French B2.

about.en:
MAiSI (Master of Arts in Sports Ethics and Integrity) is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master. Semester 1 is at KU Leuven (Belgium), semester 2 at Charles University in Prague with a summer school at the University of Peloponnese in Olympia, semester 3 at Universitat Pompeu Fabra (Barcelona) or Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz depending on the year, and the thesis semester with any partner, ending with a final Olympia summer school.

It covers anti-doping, match-fixing, safeguarding, governance and human rights in sport, and suits graduates of sport science, philosophy, law, social sciences or management aiming at sports federations, anti-doping agencies, NGOs or policy roles.

Applications opened on 8 October 2026. Erasmus Mundus scholarship applicants must apply by 1 February; self-funded non-EEA applicants by 1 April and EEA citizens by 1 July. Scholarships follow the EU standard of €1,400 a month plus participation costs.

en: Leuven, Prague, Barcelona/Mainz and Olympia
Erasmus Mundus scholarships for all nationalities
Scholarship deadline 1 February 2027

eligibility.en: Any nationality. A relevant bachelor's degree and English proficiency per KU Leuven's admission requirements for MAiSI.

en: Read the admission requirements on the MAiSI / KU Leuven pages
Prepare transcripts, CV, motivation letter and references
Apply through the KU Leuven online application and request scholarship consideration
Submit by 1 February 2027

costs.en: Erasmus Mundus scholars receive participation-cost coverage and a monthly allowance (EU standard €1,400 for up to 24 months). Self-funded fees are on the Funding Options page.

about.en:
The Amelia Earhart Fellowship, created by Zonta International in 1938 in honour of the aviator, supports women pursuing doctoral degrees in aerospace engineering and space sciences. Up to 30 fellows are chosen each year, and the award can be used at any accredited university in any country.

Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a PhD programme and have completed at least one year of it, or already hold a master's in an aerospace-applied field, and must not graduate before April 2028. Selection rests on academic record, research relevance to aerospace and recommendations.

The 2027 application must be completed online by 15 November 2026, and applicants hear back by the end of April 2027. Alumnae include astronauts, engineers and senior space-agency leaders, which makes it one of the most respected awards for women in the field.

en: US$12,000 for women PhD students in aerospace or space science
Use at any university worldwide; up to 30 fellows a year
Deadline 15 November 2026

eligibility.en: Women of any nationality enrolled full-time in a PhD/doctoral programme in aerospace engineering or space sciences (or a closely applied field) who have completed at least one year of the PhD or hold a master's in an aerospace-applied field, with a superior academic record, and who will not graduate before April 2028. Postdocs, Zonta members/employees and previous fellows are not eligible.

en: Create an account on Zonta's AwardSpring portal
Write the research and career essays and upload transcripts
Arrange recommendation letters and university verification
Submit the full application by 15 November 2026

costs.en: A one-off US$12,000 fellowship for the academic year, usable for tuition, living or research costs.

score_reason: Prestigious and global, but partial funding and only for women aerospace PhD students.

about.en:
The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship Fund, set up in 1949 by the P.E.O. Sisterhood, gives grants to women from other countries for graduate study in the United States and Canada, in the belief that education builds world peace and understanding.

Awards of up to US$12,500 go to women enrolled (or admitted) in full-time master's or doctoral programmes at accredited US or Canadian institutions who plan to return to their home country after graduating. It is a supplementary award, so most recipients combine it with university funding or other scholarships.

The online eligibility form and application open each autumn, and applications are accepted through 15 December for the following academic year.

en: Up to US$12,500 for graduate study in the US or Canada
For women from outside the US and Canada
Deadline 15 December 2026

eligibility.en: Women who are not US or Canadian citizens or permanent residents, enrolled or admitted to full-time graduate study (master's or doctorate) at an accredited college or university in the US or Canada, who intend to return home after their studies. International students at Cottey College are also eligible.

en: Open the IPS form on the P.E.O. International website
Complete the eligibility questions
If eligible, fill in the full application with financial information and references
Submit by 15 December 2026

costs.en: Up to US$12,500 per academic year; it does not cover full costs, so applicants need other funding sources.

score_reason: Helpful top-up for women already admitted in North America; not full funding.

about.en:
Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG), founded in memory of Margaret McNamara by World Bank Group families, has supported 639 women from 81 countries. Its US-Canada Program gives grants to women from developing countries who are already enrolled full-time at accredited in-person universities in the United States or Canada, in fields such as engineering, IT, health, science, education, social studies and law.

Applicants must be at least 25 at the deadline, be nationals of a country on MMEG's eligibility list, hold a valid student visa, remain enrolled for at least one semester after the award and graduate within three years. Grantees commit to working in or with developing countries to improve the lives of women and/or children.

The US-Canada window runs from 15 September to 15 January (11:59 pm EST), with results in April. MMEG also runs programmes for students in France, South Africa and Latin America with their own windows. Essays must be your own; AI-written applications are disqualified.

en: For women 25+ from developing countries studying in the US or Canada
Grants go to students who will work to improve the lives of women and children
Deadline 15 January 2027

eligibility.en: Self-identifying women aged 25 or older at the deadline, nationals of countries on the MMEG eligibility list, enrolled full-time in an accredited in-person programme in the US or Canada with a valid student visa, staying enrolled at least one semester after the award and graduating within three years. Not US/Canadian citizens or permanent residents; relatives of World Bank Group, IMF or IDB staff are excluded.

en: Read the eligibility criteria, checklist and FAQs on mmeg.org
Open the application portal and select 'US-Canada Program'
Upload every document on the checklist (incomplete applications are rejected)
Write your essays yourself and submit by 15 January 2027

costs.en: A one-time education grant; MMEG does not publish a fixed amount on its application page. It supplements other funding.

score_reason: Open now and well-targeted, but a modest top-up grant for students already in North America.

about.en:
EDISS (Engineering of Data-intensive Intelligent Software Systems) is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by Åbo Akademi University in Turku, Finland, with Mälardalen University (Västerås, Sweden), the University of the Balearic Islands (Palma, Spain) and the University of L'Aquila (Italy). Students take a common first year and choose a second-year specialisation, such as Computer Vision and Intelligent Systems in Palma.

It is for graduates with a strong university background in computer science, software engineering or applied mathematics; IT work experience does not replace that. Only TOEFL or IELTS (not online versions) are accepted, with exemptions for some English-taught degrees.

Intake 7 starts in August 2027. The Erasmus Mundus and EDISS scholarship round opens 16 November 2026 and closes 12 January 2027. EMJM scholars get a €9,000/year tuition waiver plus €1,400 a month for 24 months (total €51,600); EDISS scholars get the waiver plus €800/month in year 1 and €310/month in year 2. A later round offers tuition waivers only.

EMJM package worth €51,600; EDISS scholarships too
Scholarship deadline 12 January 2027

eligibility.en: Any nationality. Bachelor's (or equivalent) in computer science, software engineering or applied mathematics from an accredited university; TOEFL or IELTS (no online versions) unless exempt. Former Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders cannot apply for another.

Prepare transcripts, diploma, CV, motivation letter, references and TOEFL/IELTS

TFMASA (Transfers-Fluids-Materials for Aeronautics Sustainable Applications) is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in aerospace engineering. Students study fluid mechanics, heat transfer and advanced materials for sustainable aviation across the University of Bordeaux (France), UCLouvain in Louvain-la-Neuve (Belgium, semester 2) and BTU Cottbus-Senftenberg (Germany, semester 3), followed by a research or industry thesis.

It suits graduates in mechanical, aerospace, materials or energy engineering or applied physics.

The 2027–2029 call runs from 1 September to 1 December 2026 (10:00 CET) for both scholarship and self-funded candidates; late applications are rejected automatically. EMJM scholars receive €1,400 a month plus a €4,500/year contribution to participation costs paid to the programme; no nationality may take more than 10% of awards.

It builds on the long-running BDMA big-data master and offers five specialisations in data management, analytics and AI.

It welcomes computer science and related graduates. You need a bachelor's (180 ECTS) from a university listed in WHED or the THE, ARWU or QS rankings, and English at B2 (IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72). Final-year students may apply.

Scholarship applications for 2027–2029 close on 11 January 2027 (12:00 GMT, strict), with reference letters by 18 January. Self-funded and partial-grant applications run from 1 March to 15 May 2027 (non-EU) or 30 May 2027 (EU). Erasmus Mundus scholarships follow the EU standard of €1,400 a month plus participation costs.

summary.ar: ماجستير إيراسموس موندوس لمدة عامين في الكيمياء الخضراء والحفز بين إسبانيا والبرتغال وفرنسا وإيطاليا. تدفع المنح 1,400 يورو شهريًا وتغطي تكاليف المشاركة؛ آخر موعد 19 فبراير 2027.

about.en:
SuCat (Sustainable Catalysis) is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master run by Universitat Rovira i Virgili (Tarragona, Spain), the University of Aveiro (Portugal), the University of Poitiers (France) and the University of Padua (Italy). It trains chemists and chemical engineers in catalysis for clean energy, green chemistry and circular industrial processes, with language and culture courses included.

You need a bachelor's (Eurobachelor or equivalent, at least 180 ECTS by the start) in chemistry, biochemistry, biotechnology, chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences or applied chemistry, plus English at B2 (C1 preferred). Final-year students may apply.

Applications for 2027–2029 run from 23 October 2026 to 19 February 2027. Across four cohorts the programme offers 34 partner-country and 16 programme-country Erasmus Mundus scholarships plus 18 NDICI and 2 IPA scholarships: €1,400 a month for up to 24 months, with participation costs (€9,000/year for partner-country students) covered.

en: Chemistry and catalysis in four countries
About 70 scholarships across four cohorts
Deadline 19 February 2027

eligibility.en: Any nationality. Bachelor's in chemistry, biochemistry, biotechnology, chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences or applied chemistry (180 ECTS before the course starts); English B2 (C1 preferred) by test or English-medium instruction. No more than about 10% of scholarships per nationality.

en: Read the how-to-apply page and FAQ
Prepare transcripts, diploma (or expected graduation proof), CV, motivation letter, English proof and references
Submit the application in English between 23 October 2026 and 19 February 2027

costs.en: Participation costs: €9,000/year (partner country) or €4,500/year (programme country), covered for scholarship holders. Scholarship living allowance: €1,400 per month for up to 24 months. Living costs: about €600–1,000/month depending on city.

score_reason: Good number of scholarships and a late deadline for chemistry graduates.

summary.en: Monthly scholarships from the Rosa Luxemburg Foundation for international master's and PhD students at German universities who combine strong grades with political and social engagement. German at B2 level is required.
summary.ka: Rosa Luxemburg Foundation-ის ყოველთვიური სტიპენდიები გერმანიის უნივერსიტეტების უცხოელი მაგისტრანტებისა და დოქტორანტებისთვის, რომლებიც კარგ აკადემიურ შედეგებს პოლიტიკურ და საზოგადოებრივ აქტივობას უთავსებენ. საჭიროა გერმანული B2 დონეზე.
summary.ar: منح شهرية من مؤسسة روزا لوكسمبورغ لطلاب الماجستير والدكتوراه الدوليين في الجامعات الألمانية الذين يجمعون بين التفوق الأكاديمي والنشاط السياسي والاجتماعي. يُشترط مستوى B2 في الألمانية.

about.en:
The Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung, a German political foundation linked to the left, funds students and doctoral candidates through its Studienwerk. International master's students enrolled at a state or state-recognised German university can receive study scholarships if they plan to return home afterwards; doctoral candidates of any nationality accepted at a German university can be funded, usually for three years (medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine excluded).

Selection looks at academic excellence, political and social engagement in line with the foundation's aims (social justice, democracy, anti-discrimination), German at B2 or higher, and personal or family background, with priority for under-represented groups.

Applications are online only. The annual deadline is 1 October, for funding starting in the following summer semester; the 2026 round has closed, so the next deadline is 1 October 2027. Amounts follow German federal scholarship rates and are listed on the German-language application page.

en: Monthly stipend for master's and PhD students in Germany
Values-based selection: social and political engagement
Annual deadline 1 October

eligibility.en: Master's: international (including EU) students enrolled at a German state or state-recognised university who plan to return home. PhD: domestic and international candidates in any field except medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine, accepted by a German university. German at B2 or above, strong grades and demonstrable engagement.

en: Read the eligibility rules on the German application page (rosalux.de/stiftung/studienwerk/stipendienbewerbung)
Enrol at (or be accepted by) a German university
Prepare CV, motivation letter, transcripts, references and proof of engagement
Apply online before 1 October (no postal applications)

costs.en: Monthly stipend at German federal scholarship rates (amounts on the German application page), plus the foundation's seminar programme. Tuition-free study at German public universities usually means fees are only the semester contribution.

score_reason: Real funding but next deadline is October 2027 and German B2 is required.

summary.ka: ორწლიანი Erasmus Mundus მაგისტრატურა კიბერუსაფრთხოებაში ჩრდილოეთ ევროპის, ესტონეთის, საფრანგეთისა და ავსტრიის შვიდ წამყვან ტექნიკურ უნივერსიტეტში. Erasmus Mundus სტიპენდია წელიწადში €16,800-ს იხდის; განაცხადი 2026 წლის 16 ნოემბრიდან 2027 წლის 4 იანვრამდე.
summary.ar: ماجستير إيراسموس موندوس لمدة عامين في الأمن السيبراني عبر سبع جامعات تقنية رائدة في دول الشمال الأوروبي وإستونيا وفرنسا والنمسا. تدفع منحة إيراسموس موندوس 16,800 يورو سنويًا؛ التقديم من 16 نوفمبر 2026 إلى 4 يناير 2027.

about.en:
CyberSURE is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in cybersecurity and assurance that combines practical security engineering with a research-based curriculum. The consortium is NTNU (Norway, coordinator in Trondheim), Aalto University (Finland), KTH (Sweden), DTU (Denmark), the University of Tartu (Estonia), EURECOM (France) and TU Graz (Austria), with industry partners such as the Norwegian Cyber Range.

It suits computer science, computer engineering and related graduates aiming at security engineering, assurance, cryptography or research careers.

The 2027 intake application opens on 16 November 2026 and closes on 4 January 2027 (23:59 GMT+1); English test results must arrive by 18 January. You choose the scholarship type in the application form. In the 2026 intake, up to 18 Erasmus Mundus scholarships were awarded (12 open to all countries, 5 for targeted regions), each worth €16,800 a year for travel, visa, installation and living costs.

en: Seven leading tech universities (NTNU, Aalto, KTH, DTU, Tartu, EURECOM, TU Graz)
Erasmus Mundus scholarship €16,800/year
Apply 16 Nov 2026 – 4 Jan 2027

eligibility.en: Any nationality. Bachelor's in computer science, computer engineering or a closely related field and English proficiency, per the admission page. Former Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders cannot receive another EMJM scholarship.

en: Read the how-to-apply page for the 2027 intake
Prepare transcripts, diploma, CV, motivation letter and references
Submit the online application between 16 November 2026 and 4 January 2027 and choose your scholarship type
Upload English test results by 18 January 2027

costs.en: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: €16,800 per year (2026 rate) toward travel, visa, installation and subsistence, with participation costs covered. Self-funded students pay participation costs listed on the scholarships and fees page.

score_reason: Hot field, elite universities, clear upcoming window.

name.ar: منحة KTH لدراسة الماجستير (خريف 2027)

summary.en: KTH in Stockholm waives the full tuition fee for a small number of top fee-paying students in its one- and two-year master's programmes. Apply by 15 January 2027 after applying to the programme as your first choice.
summary.ka: სტოკჰოლმის KTH სრულად ათავისუფლებს სწავლის საფასურისგან მცირე რაოდენობის საუკეთესო ფასიან სტუდენტს ერთ- და ორწლიან სამაგისტრო პროგრამებზე. განაცხადი 2027 წლის 15 იანვრამდე, მას შემდეგ რაც პროგრამას პირველ არჩევანად მიუთითებ.
summary.ar: تعفي جامعة KTH في ستوكهولم عددًا محدودًا من أفضل الطلاب الدافعين للرسوم من رسوم برامج الماجستير لمدة عام أو عامين بالكامل. قدّم قبل 15 يناير 2027 بعد اختيار البرنامج كخيارك الأول.

about.en:
KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm is Sweden's largest technical university. The KTH Scholarship covers the full tuition fee for a one- or two-year master's programme (the second year depends on satisfactory first-year results). It does not cover living costs.

It is for fee-paying (mostly non-EU/EEA) students who rank a KTH master's programme as their first priority on universityadmissions.se and pay the application fee. Joint Erasmus+/EIT programmes and Computer Simulations for Science and Engineering are excluded. The scholarship form asks how you plan to contribute to sustainable development with your KTH degree; your admission documents are used for evaluation.

For autumn 2027, the scholarship application opens on 1 December 2026 and closes on 15 January 2027, documents must be on universityadmissions.se by 1 February, and results come on 1 April 2027. In the 2026 cycle, 65 of 718 admitted applicants (about 9%) were nominated.

en: Full tuition waiver for the whole master's
Engineering, computer science, architecture and more
Apply 1 Dec 2026 – 15 Jan 2027

eligibility.en: Fee-paying students (usually non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens) who apply to a KTH master's programme as first priority on universityadmissions.se, pay the application fee and meet the programme's admission requirements. Not for joint Erasmus+/EIT programmes or COSSE. Open to Georgian and Qatari citizens.

en: Apply to a KTH master's programme as your first priority on universityadmissions.se (by 15 January 2027)
Pay the application fee
Fill in the KTH scholarship form between 1 December 2026 and 15 January 2027, including your sustainability statement
Upload all programme documents to universityadmissions.se by 1 February 2027

costs.en: Covers the full KTH tuition fee for one or two years. Living costs in Stockholm (roughly SEK 10,000–12,000 per month) are not covered.

score_reason: Full tuition at a top tech university with a clear window; living costs extra.

name.ka: Aalto University-ის ექსელენს სტიპენდია (მაგისტრატურა, 2027 წლის შემოდგომა)

summary.en: Aalto University in Finland waives 100% of tuition for top fee-paying master's applicants in business, technology, and art and design. You ask for it in the master's application, open 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027.
summary.ka: ფინეთის Aalto University სწავლის საფასურისგან 100%-ით ათავისუფლებს საუკეთესო ფასიან მაგისტრანტებს ბიზნესის, ტექნოლოგიისა და ხელოვნება-დიზაინის მიმართულებით. სტიპენდიას მაგისტრატურის განაცხადშივე ითხოვ, რომელიც 2026 წლის 7 დეკემბრიდან 2027 წლის 5 იანვრამდეა ღია.
