about.en:
Aalto University in Espoo, near Helsinki, is Finland's leading university for technology, business, and art and design. Its Excellence Scholarship is a full (100%) tuition-fee waiver for the two-year normative length of a master's degree, awarded to the strongest fee-paying applicants in each programme.

It is for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who must pay tuition. There is no separate form: you answer 'yes' to the scholarship question in your Studyinfo.fi master's application, and decisions come with admission results. Programmes may decide not to award any, and the scholarship does not cover living costs (at least €800 a month).

For autumn 2027, the application period runs from 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027, with documents due by 12 January 2027. Non-EU applicants pay a €100 application fee; some programmes need GMAT/GRE or language test scores.

en: 100% tuition waiver for two years
Technology, business, art and design
Apply 7 Dec 2026 – 5 Jan 2027

eligibility.en: Tuition-fee-liable applicants (non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens without a fee-exempting residence permit) applying to an Aalto master's programme. Merit-based and highly competitive. Applicants admitted from the waiting list cannot get the scholarship. Open to Georgian and Qatari citizens.

en: Read the application instructions and your programme's evaluation criteria
Take any required language/GMAT/GRE tests in time for scores to arrive
Fill in the Studyinfo.fi application between 7 December 2026 and 5 January 2027 and answer 'yes' to the scholarship question
Pay the €100 application fee within seven days
Upload all documents by 12 January 2027

costs.en: Covers 100% of tuition for the normative study time. Living costs (at least €800/month) and the €100 application fee are your responsibility.

score_reason: Full tuition waiver at a top Nordic university; short winter window.

summary.ka: წელიწადში €7,500 ორი წლის განმავლობაში დაახლოებით 35 საუკეთესო სტუდენტისთვის TU/e-ის მიკროჩიპების ტექნოლოგიასთან დაკავშირებულ სამაგისტრო პროგრამებზე, როგორიცაა ელექტროინჟინერია, გამოყენებითი ფიზიკა, ხელოვნური ინტელექტი და ჩაშენებული სისტემები. ვადა 2027 წლის 1 იანვარია.
summary.ar: 7,500 يورو سنويًا لمدة عامين لنحو 35 من أفضل الطلاب في برامج ماجستير جامعة آيندهوفن المرتبطة بتقنية الرقائق، مثل الهندسة الكهربائية والفيزياء التطبيقية والذكاء الاصطناعي والأنظمة المدمجة. آخر موعد 1 يناير 2027.

about.en:
Eindhoven University of Technology sits in the Brainport region next to ASML, NXP and Philips, Europe's microchip heartland. The TU/e Scholarship for Excellence supports about 35 highly talented master's students a year (20 EEA, 15 non-EEA) in programmes tied to chip innovation: Applied Physics, AI and Engineering Systems, Automotive Technology, Computer Science and Engineering (Cybersecurity, Systems & AI tracks), Data Science and AI, Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Industrial and Applied Mathematics (quantum and AI tracks), Mechanical Engineering (Aerospace Systems), Nuclear Fusion, Sustainable Energy Technology, and Systems and Control.

The award is €7,500 a year for two years, paid monthly; non-EEA winners may receive part of it through the NL Scholarship in year one. You need a GPA of at least 7.5/10 and must not have studied in the Netherlands before. It is very competitive (about 2% of applicants).

You indicate interest and add a short motivation in your master's application, which must be complete by 1 January 2027. Results come by the end of March 2027.

en: €7,500/year for 2 years
Chip-related programmes in Europe's semiconductor hub
Deadline 1 January 2027

eligibility.en: International (EEA and non-EEA) applicants to an eligible full-time TU/e master's starting 1 September 2027, with a non-Dutch diploma, no prior Dutch higher education, GPA ≥ 7.5/10 and able to meet Dutch visa rules. JADS and European double-degree programmes excluded.

en: Apply to an eligible TU/e master's programme or track
State in the application that you want to be considered and add a short motivation
Make sure the application is complete by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET

costs.en: €7,500 per academic year for two years (second year requires 45 ECTS in year 1). Non-EEA tuition and living costs are much higher, so you must show sufficient funds for the visa.

score_reason: Partial award, very selective, but a near deadline in a strong field.

summary.ka: ჟენევის Graduate Institute მაგისტრანტებს წელიწადში CHF 20,000-მდე სრულ ან ნაწილობრივ სტიპენდიას აძლევს, ყველა მიღებულ დოქტორანტს კი ოთხწლიან პაკეტს. განაცხადი ფინანსური დახმარების მოთხოვნით 2027 წლის 14 იანვრამდე.

about.en:
The Geneva Graduate Institute (IHEID) is a leading school of international relations, international law, economics, development and anthropology, in the heart of International Geneva alongside the UN and hundreds of NGOs.

Master's applicants can request need- and merit-based aid in the same application: a full or partial scholarship (maximum CHF 20,000 a year for two years) and/or a tuition reduction on fees of CHF 8,000 a year for non-residents. Stipend holders must live in Switzerland or neighbouring France, and second-year students reapply in spring. Every PhD offer includes a four-year package, generally CHF 20,000 a year plus reduced tuition, or a research-assistant position or external foundation funding.

For September 2027 entry, the main deadline for all master's and PhD programmes is 14 January 2027 (references by 22 January). Master's financial aid can only be requested in this January round; there is no later chance.

en: Master's aid up to CHF 20,000/year + tuition reductions
Every PhD offer includes a four-year package
Deadline 14 January 2027

eligibility.en: Applicants of any nationality to IHEID master's or PhD programmes. Master's aid is based on academic excellence, financial need and available funds (proof of income, tax and bank statements required). One application per cycle.

en: Choose your master's or PhD programme
Fill in the online application and, for master's, the financial-aid section with income and bank documents
Pay the CHF 100 fee and submit by 14 January 2027
Make sure recommendation letters arrive by 22 January 2027

costs.en: Master's tuition CHF 8,000/year (non-residents). Aid: up to CHF 20,000/year scholarship and/or tuition reduction. PhD: about CHF 20,000/year (CHF 2,000/month, Sept–June) with tuition of CHF 3,000 in year 1 and CHF 1,000 thereafter. Geneva living costs are high (about CHF 2,000+/month).

score_reason: Strong aid for IR/development in Geneva; deadline 14 January.

about.en:
The Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation (ITC) at the University of Twente is a world centre for remote sensing, GIS and spatial planning, with a long history of training professionals from developing countries.

The ITC Excellence Scholarship gives €25,000 plus an ITC tuition waiver of €33,180 for the two-year Master's in Geo-information Science and Earth Observation or the Master's in Spatial Engineering. It is partial: with total costs estimated at €75,680, you contribute about €17,500 for the rest of tuition, living allowance, insurance and residence permit. To continue into year two, you need at least 45 of 60 EC.

Applicants must be nationals and residents of one of about 150 eligible countries, be in the top 10% academically, have IELTS 6.5 and hold academic admission before applying. The 2027 application deadline is 1 March 2027.

en: €25,000 scholarship + €33,180 tuition waiver
Remote sensing, GIS and spatial engineering
Deadline 1 March 2027

eligibility.en: Nationals and residents of an eligible country (about 150, including Afghanistan, Brazil, India, Kenya, Mexico, Nigeria, Ukraine and Vietnam; check the list for Georgia), academic admission to the eligible ITC master's, non-Dutch bachelor's, top 10% of class, IELTS 6.5 overall, first enrolment at UT, ability to pay the own contribution, and no other full scholarship.

en: Apply for academic admission to the ITC master's via the UT online system
Wait for the acceptance letter
Complete the ITC Excellence Scholarship form with required documents
Submit by 1 March 2027 and plan for the €17,500 own contribution

costs.en: Scholarship €25,000 + tuition waiver €33,180. Own contribution about €17,500 (tuition remainder, living, insurance, residence permit) of an estimated €75,680 total for two years.

score_reason: Substantial award for a niche field, but requires a sizeable own contribution.

about.en:
The Swedish Institute's Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship funds women with leadership experience to take selected English-taught STEM master's programmes at Swedish universities. It is separate from the SI Scholarship for Global Professionals and targets ten countries: Bangladesh, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Nigeria, the Philippines, Rwanda, South Africa, Thailand and Vietnam.

The scholarship pays full tuition directly to the university, a monthly allowance of SEK 12,000 and a one-off travel grant of SEK 15,000, plus membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals. Applicants need documented work and leadership experience (from a job, entrepreneurship or civil society) and must not already hold an SI scholarship or a Swedish degree.

The process has two steps: apply to an eligible master's on universityadmissions.se between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027, then submit the SI application between 8 and 24 February 2027. The list of eligible programmes and application documents is published on 13 November 2026.

en: Full tuition + SEK 12,000/month + SEK 15,000 travel grant
For women STEM leaders from 10 African and Asian countries
SI portal open 8–24 February 2027

eligibility.en: Female citizens of Bangladesh, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Nigeria, the Philippines, Rwanda, South Africa, Thailand or Vietnam (residence elsewhere allowed), liable to pay Swedish tuition fees, applying to an eligible STEM master's, with documented work and leadership experience, and without a previous SI scholarship or Swedish degree. Not open to Georgian or Qatari citizens.

en: Check the eligible master's programmes published on 13 November 2026
Apply to the programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and keep your application number
Prepare the SI application documents listed on the SI page (including proof of work and leadership experience)
Submit the SI application between 8 and 24 February 2027 (closes 14:59 CET)

costs.en: Full tuition paid by SI to the university, SEK 12,000 per month living allowance, one-time SEK 15,000 travel grant (not for those already in Sweden), and SI network membership.

score_reason: Fully funded and open soon, but only for women from 10 countries.
